newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cash coffee markets revived by price falls.
newsitem.headline: German cash coffee markets revived by price falls.

text.p: Germany's physical coffee markets are livelier than in recent weeks because of falls in futures prices and improved roastings, traders said on Monday.
"Sales from the industry to wholesalers are picking up and retail price rises have begun to bring better sales returns," one said.
"This, together with the fall in futures, translates into more confident consumer enquiries and some purchases."
But differentials needed to come down further to attract large-scale buying, the traders added.
Mild weather in Brazil was expected to weigh on futures, with New York arabicas due to reopen trading after a public holiday on Friday.
Buying in Hamburg centred on competitive Colombians and Central Americans while Brazils were selling far more slowly.
The industry has bought sufficient from this origin in recent weeks and differentials were now unattractive, traders said.
Kenyans were not available because the country has suspended its auctions for the next two weeks.
Buyers were looking into Burundian and New Guinean coffee as replacements for Kenyans.
Robusta prices held up for now but traders here expected differentials to come under pressure from new grading criteria on London's LIFFE.
Certain volumes would not pass new grading criteria and should appear in the free market for sale.
El Salvador arabicas of the c.st. grade cost $206 per 50 kg fob, down $8 on the week, and Colombia excelso was at $201, which was down $8.
Indonesia robustas EK-1 were offered at $86 cif.
